turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes, and I'd like to know why my son found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class.
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.
Okay. What did you find, and what does it have to do with the zero?
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?
Don't manage me, Hale. You said you reread three essays, and so far you've told me nothing about what's in them. Is there a document, or not?
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.
Then why is there a zero next to his name? I'm waiting for you to tell me who decided that, and when.
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.
Don't manage me, Hale. If you care about him, withdraw the zero and tell me who decided to enter it before anyone called me.
